chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who begins her menstruation during the month of Ramadan before the sun sets. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She breaks her fast when she begins menstruating.'
ai.seo_question: Does a woman's fast break immediately if she starts menstruating during the day in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that menstruation nullifies the fast immediately upon onset, regardless of the time remaining until sunset, distinguishing it from other invalidators that require a full day's fast to be broken. It reflects the Shia juristic consensus that the state of major ritual impurity (hadath akbar) takes precedence over the obligation of fasting during daylight hours. This ruling underscores the practical flexibility in Shia fiqh, allowing women to resume eating and drinking as soon as the physical sign of menstruation appears.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ays Bin Al Qasim who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a woman who menstruated during a Month of Ramazan before the disappearance of the sun. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She would break when she menstruated’.
en.sarwar: 3. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from ‘Is ibn al-Qasim who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman who experiences Hayd (menses) in the month of Ramadan before sunset. He (the Imam) said, ‘She must stop fasting at the time she finds Hayd (menses).”’
